clue.text: Married, and said to be virtuous

parts.note: said in the sense of spoken, not written, is oral

explanation.surface: A newlywed claims, by word of mouth, to be a good person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal, but here it simply means spoken, giving ORAL after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral and virtuous are synonyms describing upright, ethical conduct.

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for split is placed around the other piece

parts.note: a split or tear is a rent
13-across is EXERCISE, and PE (physical education) is exercise

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for a tear around their workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 13 points to EXERCISE; its abbreviated synonym PE goes inside RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel remorse for something done, a verb synonym of regret.

clue.text: British money is involved in unexpected squeeze

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it, so the money letter sits within the adjective

parts.note: unexpected means strange
L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, Britain's currency

explanation.surface: Sterling gets caught up in a surprise financial squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle is to throttle, a forceful squeezing of the throat.

parts.note: reads like a traveller packing, but describes a bird grooming its feathers with its beak before taking off

explanation.surface: Someone got ready to catch a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that has preened has tidied its plumage, a natural readying before taking wing.

indicators.note: to negotiate is to work something round into a new shape, signalling rearranged letters

explanation.surface: With savings in hand, a borrower can bargain over credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiate' rearranges the eight letters of SAVED and CAN; 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are sums of money paid in anticipation, a synonym for loans.

clue.text: Many tend to make themselves heard when doing such work

definitions.text: Many tend to make themselves heard when doing such work

parts.words: Many tend to make themselves heard when doing such work
parts.note: evokes cleaners who sing or whistle as they scrub, with a hint of clans singing in the sound of the word

explanation.surface: People are often noisy while carrying out this sort of job.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning and scrubbing is the work, and people famously sing over housework.

clue.text: Nothing's right for a romantic relation!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and the possessive adds an S
a Tory is a right-wing Conservative

explanation.surface: A zero-sum political right is no basis for a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' here means a narrative or account, not a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation can mean a told account, and one about romance is a romantic tale.

clue.text: It's mature of the French filling in a junior officer

indicators.note: one piece filling another sits inside it, so the French words go into the gap

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a junior officer
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: A French officer says growing up is part of a lieutenant's job.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is fully grown, so mature describes one.

definitions.meaning: plucky, willing to go on, as in being up for a challenge
lame, as in an old-fashioned phrase for an injured leg

explanation.definitionFit: Plucky and brave is one sense; a lame or crippled limb is the other, both older idiomatic senses.

clue.text: After fifty-one censure can be made to wound

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace counts as one in cards
to rate someone is to scold or censure them

explanation.surface: Fifty-one telling-offs can cause real hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty-one' is not 51 or LI here but L and ACE; 'rate' in its old sense means scold. 'After' and 'can be made to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear flesh, a way to wound.

clue.text: A man of learning and potential in Iran

annotationWithheld.why: A man of learning and potential in Iran (6): A + BA gives ABA, but no reading of 'and potential' gives DAN, and the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: A man of learning and potential in Iran

clue.text: A large animal, yet among the most agile

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A big creature that is nevertheless one of the nimblest.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is a sizeable beast.

indicators.note: in puts the royalty letters inside the word for duty

parts.note: excise is a duty levied on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal is put through drills while on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen's cipher, a standard crossword stand-in for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is physical training and practice.

parts.note: to rein in is to control
force means power

explanation.surface: Back-up means having a grip on strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen or bolster, a synonym of support.

parts.note: sounds like builders under contract, but means tenants who hold a lease on a property

explanation.surface: Construction firms that have won a tender.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants on a lease hold a contract to occupy premises.

clue.text: A caring person taking a crook in hand

definitions.text: A caring person taking a crook in hand

parts.words: A caring person taking a crook in hand
parts.note: reads like a social worker reforming a criminal, but the crook is a hooked staff and the carer looks after sheep

explanation.surface: A kindly soul helps reform a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman tending a flock carries a hooked staff.

parts.note: to con is to deceive, so cons means deceives

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of ten may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: The deal tricks perhaps ten people.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent is permission or assent, a form of agreement.

parts.note: over means finished or past
a cast is the set of players in a show

explanation.surface: Former actors may look downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dull and gloomy.

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something new, so the letters of priests are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clergy grouped together into these groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow bands of colour.

parts.note: in means fashionable
he stands for a man or guy
rent is the old past tense of rend, meaning broke apart

explanation.surface: A fashionable fellow who is skint is just being himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like penniless, but means torn: RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inherent quality is innate or natural.

parts.note: reads like a man mingling at a party, but a name for a man is also a swirl of water

explanation.surface: A man doing the rounds at a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a man's name and also a whirling current in water.

indicators.note: behind places the abbreviation for left after the organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on finding a hearing aid forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, a lord.

clue.text: The traveller needs endless capital, no matter what

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
any means whichever, no matter what

explanation.surface: A wanderer requires limitless money regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany people are a traditionally nomadic people, often called travellers.

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railway lines
and means together with

explanation.surface: Railway lines bearing a company logo.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a manufacturer's trademark name.

clue.text: Used a club when business dropped off

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
shed means let fall or dropped

explanation.surface: Someone joined a golf club when trade fell away.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them with a cudgel.

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of American are reordered

explanation.surface: A covert US agency.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is legal Latin for held in private, hence secret.

clue.text: Transport in the Canterbury area is causing some alarm

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Canterbury is in Kent, in south-east England, abbreviated SE
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Traffic around Canterbury is worrying people.
explanation.walkthrough: Canterbury is a cathedral city in Kent, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare is a sudden fright or alarm.

indicators.note: a mistake means something gone wrong, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone phones in an error, or so it is believed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' signals the anagram of ONE, RINGS and A, which give the nine letters; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the process of thinking things through, synonym of thought.
